symptom: Users at the branch office report that large file transfers via FTP and SCP are hanging indefinitely after establishing a connection, while standard web browsing works fine.
root_cause: An MTU mismatch between the customer edge router (1500 bytes) and the provider MPLS interface (1492 bytes) is dropping large packets, and ICMP Destination Unreachable messages are being blocked, breaking Path MTU Discovery.
resolution: 1. Update the MTU on the provider-facing interface of the customer edge router to match the 1492-byte transport limit. 2. Enable TCP MSS clamping on the WAN interface to prevent oversized segment generation.

symptom: Voice over IP (VoIP) calls connect successfully, but audio drops out completely after the SIP handshake when media streams exceed standard packet sizes.
root_cause: The transport tunnel configuration has an overly restrictive MTU of 1300 bytes, but the core switch is forwarding unfragmented VoIP RTP packets sized at 1420 bytes with the DF (Don't Fragment) bit set.
resolution: 1. Adjust the tunnel interface MTU to 1450 bytes on both endpoints. 2. Verify packet flow using ICMP ping sweeps with the 'do not fragment' flag enabled.

symptom: Database replication between primary and secondary clusters is failing intermittently, throwing connection timeout errors during heavy transaction logs sync.
root_cause: The intermediate transport provider lowered the backbone circuit MTU to 1472 bytes during maintenance, while the database servers are transmitting jumbo frames set to 9000 bytes without proper fragmentation handling.
resolution: 1. Configure TCP Maximum Segment Size (MSS) adjustment on the core firewalls to 1432. 2. Notify the transport provider to restore the standard 1500-byte MTU on the virtual circuit.

symptom: Branch office users cannot access internal web applications hosted in the datacenter, though they can ping the server IP addresses successfully.
root_cause: ICMP type 3 code 4 (Fragmentation Needed and DF set) messages are being dropped by a firewall security rule, preventing PMTUD from resolving an MTU mismatch across the QinQ transport link.
resolution: 1. Modify the firewall ACLs to permit ICMP fragmentation-needed messages. 2. Configure global TCP MSS clamping on the edge gateway to enforce a maximum segment size of 1360.

symptom: Backup jobs running from the local server to the remote cloud repository fail consistently after transferring exactly 64KB of data.
root_cause: The Transport Layer Security (TLS) handshake succeeds using small packets, but the subsequent bulk data transfer utilizes large TCP windows that exceed the path MTU of 1400 caused by an unadjusted VLAN encapsulation overhead.
resolution: 1. Enable MTU path discovery diagnostics on the backup appliance. 2. Set the interface MTU explicitly to 1500 on the hypervisor virtual switches and verify trunk port configurations.

symptom: Remote desktop (RDP) sessions freeze and disconnect every few minutes when users maximize their display windows or scroll through graphic-heavy pages.
root_cause: RDP packets scale up in size and exceed the transport path MTU of 1450 bytes due to VXLAN overlay overhead that was not accounted for on the transport switch ports.
resolution: 1. Configure the transport switch trunk ports to support jumbo frames with an MTU of 1600. 2. Apply MTU 1450 to the virtual tunnel interfaces.

symptom: API integrations with external payment gateways are dropping connections randomly, resulting in failed transaction processing during peak hours.
root_cause: An MTU mismatch between the ISP handoff (1500) and the internal SD-WAN overlay (1420) causes packet drops for HTTPS POST payloads exceeding 1400 bytes.
resolution: 1. Enable MSS clamping on the SD-WAN edge appliance set to 1380. 2. Test connectivity using ping with varying packet sizes and DF bits set.

symptom: Monitoring tools show the site is reachable via ICMP ping, but SSH management sessions to core network devices drop immediately after the banner displays.
root_cause: SSH negotiates a larger packet size for interactive data streams, which fails because the transport provider's MPLS pseudo-wire has a lower MTU of 1448 bytes.
resolution: 1. Log into the device via console and adjust the transport interface MTU to 1440. 2. Implement TCP MSS adjustment on the management routing policy.

symptom: Video surveillance feeds from remote security cameras fail to stream to the central network video recorder (NVR), showing a black screen.
root_cause: High-bandwidth UDP video streams are heavily fragmented across the wireless transport bridge, which has a strict MTU limit of 1400 bytes, causing frame corruption.
resolution: 1. Lower the video encoder stream packet size configuration to output fragments under 1350 bytes. 2. Increase the wireless bridge MTU configuration to maximum allowable limits.

symptom: Users report extremely slow webpage loading speeds specifically for internal SharePoint portals, while external internet sites load instantly.
root_cause: The internal site-to-site IPsec VPN tunnel adds overhead that exceeds the transport network's physical MTU, leading to packet fragmentation drops and excessive TCP retransmissions.
resolution: 1. Configure crypto map MTU or adjust the IPsec tunnel interface MTU to 1436. 2. Enable 'ip tcp adjust-mss 1360' on the VPN termination router.

symptom: Customer reports FTTH speed test dropping below 20 Mbps on a 200 Mbps symmetrical plan during peak evening hours.
root_cause: GPON OLT upstream port congestion due to oversubscription on the local splitter during high-traffic intervals.
resolution: Migrated the customer ONT to a less congested PON port on the same OLT chassis and reallocated traffic profile.

symptom: Subscriber experiencing severe buffering on 4K video streams; optical power meter shows high attenuation on the drop fiber.
root_cause: Micro-bend in the indoor drop fiber optic cable near the wall outlet causing a 6dB signal loss.
resolution: Re-routed and re-terminated the damaged section of the indoor drop cable, restoring optimal RX optical power of -20 dBm.

symptom: Enterprise FTTH user notes throughput capped precisely at 100 Mbps despite subscribing to a 1 Gbps dedicated pipe.
root_cause: Auto-negotiation failure on the customer-premise router WAN port, forcing a fallback to Fast Ethernet speeds.
resolution: Logged into the ONT, forced the LAN port to 1000Mbps Full Duplex, and advised the customer to replace a faulty Cat5 patch cord.

symptom: Multiple FTTH subscribers in the same residential building complaining of sudden internet slowdowns and high latency.
root_cause: Macro-bend and dirty connector on the floor's multi-dwelling unit (MDU) optical splitter input.
resolution: Cleaned the MDU bulkhead adapters with an optical click cleaner and re-spliced a damaged pigtail.

symptom: Customer reports intermittent low throughput and packet loss that worsens during humid weather conditions.
root_cause: Water ingress in the outdoor aerial closure causing macro-bending and high reflection on the distribution fiber.
resolution: Replaced the damaged aerial splice closure, re-stripped and fusion-spliced the affected fibers, and sealed the enclosure.

symptom: Subscriber on a 500 Mbps FTTH plan gets maximum 80 Mbps via Wi-Fi and wired connections alike.
root_cause: Misconfigured Traffic Shaping / Quality of Service (QoS) profile applied globally to the ONT WAN interface by mistake.
resolution: Removed the legacy QoS policing rule from the ACS server configuration and pushed a clean factory profile to the ONT.

symptom: User experiences sluggish web browsing and slow file downloads; traceroute shows extreme jitter to the first gateway.
root_cause: Hardware failure on the ONT's internal PHY chip, resulting in packet corruption and TCP window throttling.
resolution: Dispatched a field technician to swap out the faulty Huawei ONT with a new unit and provisioned it via TR-069.

symptom: FTTH connection speed drops drastically whenever heavy rain occurs in the neighborhood.
root_cause: Water entering an improperly sealed underground handhole, putting mechanical pressure on loose buffer tubes.
resolution: Pumped out water from the handhole, repaired the buffer tube housing, and placed a gel-filled waterproof enclosure.

symptom: NOC alarm triggered for degraded optical signal on an entire feeder fiber, resulting in low throughput for 64 connected homes.
root_cause: Accidental fiber cut during civil roadworks partially severing the 72-fiber distribution cable.
resolution: Excavated the strike point, exposed the damaged cable, and performed an emergency mechanical restoration and temporary splice.

symptom: Subscriber notices download speeds are normal at 300 Mbps, but upload speeds never exceed 5 Mbps.
root_cause: Transmitter laser bias current degradation on the ONT optical transceiver module.
resolution: Replaced the failing ONT device and verified optical output power parameters (Tx power at +3 dBm).

symptom: Customer in Tunis reports that their primary database subnet 196.203.14.0/24 is unreachable from external networks.
root_cause: An overly restrictive prefix-list applied during a routine maintenance window blocked the outbound advertisement of the /24 prefix to upstream provider AS64500.
resolution: 1. Access the edge router and review the active route-map and prefix-list configurations. 2. Modify the prefix-list to correctly permit 196.203.14.0/24. 3. Clear BGP peer session soft inbound/outbound to force re-advertisement.

symptom: Monitoring alerts that backup MPLS site routes are missing, causing failover traffic to drop at the Sfax data center.
root_cause: The BGP session between the local PE and the provider's route reflector dropped due to keepalive timer mismatches, withdrawing all customer prefixes.
resolution: 1. Verify BGP neighbor state and check system logs for reset reasons. 2. Standardize BGP keepalive and hold-down timers with the service provider. 3. Reinstate the peering session and confirm prefix table convergence.

symptom: External partners state they cannot resolve or route traffic to our newly provisioned public IP block 41.226.12.0/22.
root_cause: The new prefix was allocated in IPAM and configured locally, but the static blackhole route required for BGP aggregation was missing from the routing table.
resolution: 1. Configure a static discard route for 41.226.12.0/22 pointing to Null0. 2. Add a 'network' statement under the BGP routing process. 3. Verify the prefix is now present in the BGP table and advertised to peers.

symptom: Branch office users in Sousse report intermittent application timeouts; traceroutes show packets stop at the border router.
root_cause: A route flap dampening penalty was incorrectly triggered on the primary transit link, suppressing the advertisement of the local /22 prefix.
resolution: 1. Check BGP dampening status for the affected prefix using 'show ip bgp dampening'. 2. Clear the dampening penalty on the core router. 3. Monitor the peer logs to ensure stability and normal advertisement resumption.

symptom: Upstream ISP notifies us that our main corporate block is missing from the global routing table, isolating public web services.
root_cause: The AS_PATH prepending policy was misconfigured with an invalid autonomous system number, causing upstream providers to drop the update via AS path loop prevention filters.
resolution: 1. Correct the route-map to use the valid local ASN for path prepending. 2. Commit the changes and clear BGP outbound to send fresh updates. 3. Check looking glasses to verify global prefix visibility.

symptom: Internal applications cannot reach external API endpoints hosted on specific partner networks.
root_cause: BGP community strings used to control regional traffic engineering were improperly stripped by an intermediate policy, causing the external routes not to be installed in the local RIB.
resolution: 1. Audit the inbound route-maps for dropped community tags. 2. Update the policy to accept and process standard transit community values. 3. Soft reset the BGP peer to rebuild the routing table.

symptom: Voice over IP (VoIP) endpoints are unreachable from external SIP trunks tied to the Nabeul gateway.
root_cause: An accidental change in the eBGP multihop configuration caused the peering session to drop, halting the propagation of the voice VLAN subnets.
resolution: 1. Restore the 'ebgp-multihop' parameter on the affected neighbor statement. 2. Verify TCP port 179 connectivity between endpoints. 3. Validate that voice prefixes are successfully re-learned.

symptom: Partner network administrators report missing routes to our secondary DNS infrastructure subnets.
root_cause: Maximum-prefix limit was reached on the peer router due to an unauthorized subnet addition, causing the session to error-disable and drop all advertised prefixes.
resolution: 1. Review and appropriately increase the maximum-prefix threshold with the peer administrator. 2. Bring the BGP session back up using 'clear ip bgp'. 3. Monitor prefix counts to ensure they remain within the new agreed limits.

symptom: Data replication traffic between Tunis-01 and Tunis-02 fails over the WAN, throwing routing unreachable errors.
root_cause: OSPF-to-BGP redistribution was disrupted because a matching route-map tag was removed during a security audit, omitting internal /24 prefixes from being injected into BGP.
resolution: 1. Update the redistribution configuration under the BGP process to include the necessary route-map criteria. 2. Execute 'clear ip bgp *' to refresh internal BGP (iBGP) updates. 3. Confirm end-to-end route visibility.

symptom: Sfax-01 facility experiences complete loss of external connectivity for guest Wi-Fi networks.
root_cause: An inadvertent change to the AS path access-list blocked outbound advertisements for the guest network subnet range.
resolution: 1. Inspect the access-list defining permitted advertised prefixes. 2. Remove the blocking entry and apply the corrected ACL. 3. Verify advertisement status using 'show ip bgp neighbors advertised-routes'.

symptom: Customer reports intermittent internet drops every 10 to 15 minutes throughout the day, forcing manual ONT reboots to restore connectivity.
root_cause: High optical attenuation (-28.5 dBm) caused by a micro-bend in the indoor drop cable near the wall outlet.
resolution: Re-routed and replaced the damaged section of the indoor drop cable, reducing the optical loss to -18.2 dBm and stabilizing the signal.

symptom: NOC alerts show rapid flapping of the PON interface on the OLT for multiple subscribers in the same residential block, resulting in frequent session drops.
root_cause: Micro-fracture on the distribution fiber strand inside aerial closure #14 due to thermal expansion and wind stress.
resolution: Spliced the damaged distribution fiber inside the aerial closure and secured the slack storage basket to prevent further tension.

symptom: Customer experiences random Wi-Fi and wired disconnections during peak evening hours, complaining that the PON light on the ONT intermittently flashes red.
root_cause: Faulty 12V power supply unit (PSU) delivering fluctuating voltage, causing the ONT to randomly reboot under load.
resolution: Replaced the defective power supply unit with a new manufacturer-approved 12V adapter and verified stable power output.

symptom: Multiple users report total loss of synchronization and frequent dropouts starting immediately after a heavy rainstorm.
root_cause: Water ingress inside the outdoor splitter cabinet (ODC-03) leading to severe connector contamination and high reflection.
resolution: Cleaned the contaminated SC/APC patch cords and bulkhead adapters with optical cleaning solvent, and resealed the cabinet gasket.

symptom: Subscriber notes that the FTTH connection drops precisely when making heavy upstream transfers, requiring a physical power cycle of the gateway.
root_cause: Outdated ONT firmware causing a memory leak and subsequent kernel panic during high burst traffic conditions.
resolution: Upgraded the ONT firmware to version 4.12.0 via the TR-069 ACS server and performed a stress test to confirm stability.

symptom: Customer states the internet connection degrades and drops completely every afternoon as ambient temperatures rise.
root_cause: Dirty optical connector at the Floor Distribution Box (FDB) causing high insertion loss that exceeds the transceiver margin when the cable expands.
resolution: Inspected the fiber end-face with a digital microscope, cleaned it with a one-click cleaner, and re-tested insertion loss to meet standards.

symptom: NOC ticketing system receives automated alerts for persistent LOS (Loss of Signal) and frequent re-ranging events for a dedicated enterprise FTTH customer.
root_cause: Loose mechanical splice connector inside the customer premises ONT patch panel, causing intermittent physical contact loss.
resolution: Removed the faulty mechanical splice, stripped the fiber, and performed a fusion splice inside the wall outlet box.

symptom: User reports sporadic drops in connection accompanied by severe packet loss and high latency spikes before going completely down.
root_cause: Rogue ONT on the PON tree transmitting out of time slot due to a hardware failure, disrupting upstream TDMA communications for adjacent users.
resolution: Identified the rogue ONT via OLT diagnostic logs, isolated the specific subscriber line, and dispatched a technician to replace the faulty CPE.

symptom: Customer complains of random nightly disconnections where the LOS indicator turns solid red for a few minutes before reconnecting automatically.
root_cause: Interference caused by rodent damage chewing through the outer protective sheath of the direct-buried drop cable, exposing the bare fiber to soil pressure.
resolution: Excavated the damaged section of the direct-buried cable, installed a protective conduit, and spliced in a new cable segment.

symptom: Subscriber reports frequent dropped PPPoE sessions throughout the day despite the ONT showing a stable green PON status light.
root_cause: RADIUS authentication timeout issues and ARP cache table corruption on the local Broadband Remote Access Server (BRAS).
resolution: Cleared the stale ARP entries on the BRAS interface, rebooted the RADIUS session daemon, and verified stable session persistence.

symptom: Customers on the Tunis-01 border router are reporting massive packet loss and reaching European destinations via an unexpected transit provider instead of the primary peering link.
root_cause: A downstream customer enterprise network improperly re-advertised full BGP tables received from us back out to their secondary upstream, creating an unauthorized transit path.
resolution: Contacted the offending customer to filter their BGP announcements, applied strict AS-path prepending filters on our edge interfaces, and verified route preference convergence.

symptom: Monitoring alerts at Sfax-01 show a sudden spike in traffic volume crossing our backup backup satellite link, accompanied by latency degradation for local subnets.
root_cause: An upstream peer accidentally leaked our internal /20 prefix to a Tier-1 provider, causing asymmetric routing and pulling inbound traffic through a suboptimal path.
resolution: Notified the peer NOC via out-of-band channels to withdraw the leaked prefix, and implemented strict max-prefix limits and out-bound route filters on the peering session.

symptom: Internal services hosted at Sousse-01 are intermittently unreachable from external networks, and traceroutes show packets looping between our border and an adjacent ISP.
root_cause: A misconfigured route-map on our edge router stripped community tags, allowing private customer routes to leak into the global routing table.
resolution: Rolled back the latest route-map update on the border router, re-applied the standard BGP community scrub policies, and cleared the BGP session.

symptom: Bizerte-01 NOC dashboard indicates a massive influx of external traffic destined for non-existent IP addresses, threatening core router CPU utilization.
root_cause: An external Autonomous System leaked a default route (0.0.0.0/0) into their eBGP advertisement toward us, which was incorrectly accepted due to missing inbound policy validation.
resolution: Applied immediate drop policies for default routes on all edge peering sessions and updated the prefix-list policy to strictly permit only authorized customer blocks.

symptom: Gabes-01 edge routers are experiencing high memory utilization, and BGP convergence times have increased drastically following a maintenance window.
root_cause: A lateral peering partner leaked the entire global internet routing table to us, overwhelming the RIB memory limits on our edge node.
resolution: Hard-shut the affected peering session, coordinated with the partner to fix their export filters, and re-established the session with strict inbound prefix limits enforced.

symptom: Users in Nabeul-01 report that traffic to specific cloud providers is timing out, while other destinations remain accessible.
root_cause: A regional transit provider accepted a leaked route from a malicious actor, resulting in a localized BGP hijack affecting cloud subnet reachability.
resolution: Switched default static routes to backup transit provider, filed an IR incident report with the upstream transit provider, and monitored BGP path updates until resolved.

symptom: Kairouan-01 local NOC reported that outbound traffic destined for North American networks is suddenly taking an abnormally circuitous path through Asia.
root_cause: An internal router inadvertently leaked domestic enterprise routes to an international research network peering link due to an absent AS-path access list.
resolution: Updated the export filter prefix-lists on the Kairouan-01 border router to explicitly block enterprise customer ASNs from being announced to the research network.

symptom: Tunis-02 secondary transit link is completely saturated, triggering automated failover alerts and service degradation for voice-over-IP platforms.
root_cause: A third-party IXP participant leaked our more-specific /24 routes, causing traffic destined for our data center to funnel through an unintended, low-capacity port.
resolution: Contacted the IXP route server administrators to remove the leaked entries, and implemented local preference overrides to prefer direct direct-connect circuits.

symptom: Sfax-01 operations report intermittent connection drops for remote branch offices connecting via MPLS-over-BGP architecture.
root_cause: A routing loop formed because a branch office router leaked MPLS VPN labels and associated routes back into the public internet table via a misconfigured dual-home setup.
resolution: Isolated the affected branch office site by disabling the backup interface, corrected the VRF route-target export policies, and restored stable connectivity.

symptom: Critical alarms fired at Bizerte-01 regarding unauthorized transit usage, showing heavy traffic flows originating from unassigned internal ranges.
root_cause: A testing department lab network leaked internal RFC 1918 space into the eBGP feed due to a missing 'no export' community attribute on experimental route announcements.
resolution: Disconnected the lab switch uplink temporarily, added a policy rule to drop private IP spaces on all outbound eBGP policies, and re-enabled the port safely.

symptom: Users at the site are reporting extremely slow web browsing and intermittent timeouts when accessing internal applications by hostname.
root_cause: The primary on-premise DNS forwarder was misconfigured to query an unresponsive external recursive resolver, causing continuous query timeouts and fallbacks.
resolution: Updated the forwarder IP configuration in BIND to point to the resilient enterprise secondary DNS pool and restarted the named service.

symptom: Applications are experiencing high latency during startup due to delayed DNS resolution of external API endpoints.
root_cause: EDNS0 buffer size mismatches caused UDP DNS queries to exceed the MTU, forcing TCP fallbacks that drastically increased lookup times.
resolution: Adjusted the max-udp-size parameter in the local DNS caching daemon and verified path MTU discovery on the local gateway.

symptom: Employees report that internal intranet pages take up to 15 seconds to begin loading in the morning.
root_cause: The local DNS cache had been completely flushed overnight, and the authoritative nameserver for the internal zone was throttling incoming requests due to a lack of rate-limiting exceptions.
resolution: Whitelisted the local caching resolver IP on the authoritative nameserver and increased the negative caching TTL to absorb morning request spikes.

symptom: Critical database replication services are throwing connection warnings due to slow hostname resolution between cluster nodes.
root_cause: A failing network interface card on the secondary local DNS server caused packet drops and forced queries to route over a congested backup trunk.
resolution: Rerouted DNS traffic exclusively to the primary local resolver and scheduled an emergency hardware replacement for the faulty NIC.

symptom: Users attempting to access cloud-hosted productivity tools experience erratic resolution delays, sometimes failing entirely.
root_cause: ISP-provided DNS resolvers assigned via DHCP were experiencing severe packet loss over the last-mile fiber connection.
resolution: Overrode DHCP DNS settings on the local core switch to statically assign redundant public cloud resolver IPs.

symptom: Branch office personnel note that resolving external domain names takes noticeably longer than usual, impacting workflow.
root_cause: DNS query logs filled the local appliance disk to 100 capacity, causing severe I/O bottlenecks that delayed query processing.
resolution: Cleared stale log files, enabled automated log rotation, and configured a remote syslog server to offload future writes.

symptom: Finance department staff report sluggish response times when logging into the enterprise financial portal.
root_cause: Geo-proximity DNS routing was failing due to outdated subnet mapping data on the local caching server, directing traffic to a distant CDN node.
resolution: Manually purged the resolver cache and updated the geo-IP database package on the local DNS appliance.

symptom: Intermittent DNS lookup failures and high latency are affecting point-of-sale terminals across the facility.
root_cause: An asymmetric routing loop caused by a recent firewall rule change introduced high latency for DNS traffic traversing the security inspection zone.
resolution: Modified firewall policy routes to ensure symmetric return paths for all UDP port 53 traffic originating from the POS VLAN.

symptom: Developers report that Git and container registry pulls are timing out or taking minutes to resolve domain names.
root_cause: DNSSEC validation was failing on multiple zones due to a system clock drift of over 12 minutes on the local nameserver.
resolution: Synchronized the local server time using the corporate NTP pool and forced a manual validation check of the affected DNS zones.

symptom: Helpdesk is receiving calls about delayed page loads and 'Server DNS Address Could Not Be Found' errors.
root_cause: The local recursive resolver's thread pool was exhausted due to a localized DNS amplification query storm from a compromised workstation.
resolution: Isolated the compromised host using network access control, flushed the resolver queues, and applied strict rate-limiting rules.

symptom: Users at the Tunis office are unable to resolve internal application hostnames, resulting in connection timeouts when accessing the intranet.
root_cause: The primary internal DNS forwarder was unresponsive due to a memory leak in the BIND service daemon.
resolution: Restarted the BIND service on the primary DNS server and verified zone synchronization with the secondary server.

symptom: Multiple workstations in the accounting department are failing to resolve external domains, while internal services remain accessible.
root_cause: An incorrect static IP configuration pushed via DHCP assigned an invalid secondary public DNS server address.
resolution: Updated the DHCP scope options to distribute correct upstream public DNS resolvers and forced an IP lease renewal on affected machines.

symptom: External clients report intermittent failures when attempting to resolve the company's public-facing e-commerce portal.
root_cause: Expired DNSSEC cryptographic keys on the authoritative nameserver caused validating resolvers to drop the zone responses as untrusted.
resolution: Generated a new Key Signing Key (KSK) and Zone Signing Key (ZSK), then updated DS records at the domain registrar.

symptom: Branch office users cannot access newly provisioned cloud resources because hostnames return NXDOMAIN errors.
root_cause: Conditional forwarding rules for the new cloud VPC domain were omitted from the local site's caching DNS appliance.
resolution: Added a new conditional forwarder zone on the local DNS server pointing to the cloud provider's resolver endpoints.

symptom: Complete DNS resolution outage affecting all endpoints at the site, preventing any internet or local network navigation.
root_cause: A physical fiber cut severed the dedicated link connecting the local caching resolvers to the core enterprise network.
resolution: Rerouted DNS traffic over the backup SD-WAN tunnel and coordinated with the carrier to dispatch a repair crew for the severed line.

symptom: Developers report that DNS queries for staging environments are timing out or returning stale IP addresses.
root_cause: Corrupted local DNS cache records on the regional server were holding onto outdated TTL values from a decommissioned cluster.
resolution: Flushed the local DNS resolver cache using the appropriate management utility and verified immediate retrieval of fresh records.

symptom: Authentication services are failing globally for site users because domain controllers cannot be located via DNS SRV records.
root_cause: An improper ACL rule on the perimeter firewall blocked incoming and outgoing UDP/TCP port 53 traffic for the primary DC's IP.
resolution: Modified the firewall rulebase to explicitly permit DNS traffic for the domain controller subnet and verified SRV record queries.

symptom: Engineers notice slow page load times and intermittent 'Server Not Found' errors when browsing specific partner network domains.
root_cause: Rate-limiting policies implemented by the upstream ISP's recursive resolvers were dropping excessive concurrent DNS queries from our NAT pool.
resolution: Configured local DNS response rate limiting (RRL) and established traffic shaping to stay below the ISP's query threshold.

symptom: New workstations deployed in the engineering lab fail to join the Active Directory domain due to DNS lookup failures.
root_cause: The switch port VLAN assignment was incorrect, placing the lab machines on an isolated guest network that blocks internal DNS queries.
resolution: Reconfigured the switch port to the proper corporate VLAN and verified successful resolution of '_ldap._tcp.dc._msdcs' records.

symptom: Monitoring alerts show that DNS zone transfers are failing between the master nameserver and the regional slave server.
root_cause: A recent security policy update accidentally revoked the TSIG key authentication credentials used for secure zone transfers.
resolution: Re-imported the matching TSIG keys on both the master and slave DNS servers and successfully triggered a manual zone transfer.

symptom: Multiple users in the business district report intermittent 5G latency spikes reaching up to 800ms during peak hours, severely impacting video conferencing.
root_cause: The local gNodeB experienced backhaul congestion due to an unexpected surge in local enterprise traffic, exhausting the primary IPsec tunnel bandwidth.
resolution: Re-routed overflow traffic over the secondary microwave backhaul link.
Adjusted QoS profile weights for enterprise traffic classes.
Initiated capacity upgrade planning for the primary fiber backhaul.

symptom: Subscribers near the industrial port area are experiencing constant 4G ping spikes and packet loss, making remote machine telemetry unresponsive.
root_cause: A misconfigured core network GTP-U tunnel caused packets to take an suboptimal routing path through a distant regional gateway.
resolution: Updated the UPF routing tables to direct traffic through the local User Plane Function.
Flushed the GTP-U tunnel states and verified end-to-end latency.

symptom: A university campus zone reports sluggish 5G data rates and high latency specifically on the n78 frequency band.
root_cause: Severe co-channel interference caused by an uncoordinated neighboring macro cell deploying the same physical cell ID (PCI) modulo-3 pattern.
resolution: Executed an automated PCI re-planning script for the affected sector.
Optimized antenna mechanical tilt to reduce overlapping signal propagation.

symptom: Coastal tourists and residents are complaining of high 4G browsing latency and frequent TCP timeouts during evening hours.
root_cause: Radio Resource Control (RRC) state machine misconfiguration kept connected UEs in a congested scheduling queue longer than necessary.
resolution: Tuned the inactivity timer thresholds for Fast Dormancy.
Upgraded the baseband unit (BBU) firmware to the latest stability release.

symptom: Residential users report sudden latency degradation on 5G NSA (Non-Standalone) connections, dropping from 20ms to over 300ms.
root_cause: An anchor 4G eNodeB experienced heavy control-plane CPU load, causing significant handover delays to the 5G gNodeB master cell.
resolution: Restarted the control plane daemon on the eNodeB baseband card.
Offloaded 50% of RRC connections to an adjacent cell using mobility load balancing (MLB).

symptom: Emergency services and local businesses report intermittent high latency on the dedicated 4G public safety slice.
root_cause: Packet loss on the fronthaul optical fiber between the baseband unit and the remote radio head (RRH) introduced retransmission delays.
resolution: Cleaned and re-seated the SFP+ optical transceivers on both ends of the fronthaul link.
Verified bit error rate (BER) metrics returned to normal thresholds.

symptom: Shoppers in the central commercial mall note that 5G data applications suffer from high latency and buffering despite full signal bars.
root_cause: Internal DAS (Distributed Antenna System) optical master unit had a failing power supply unit, causing micro-drops and packet queuing.
resolution: Replaced the faulty power supply unit in the DAS master rack.
Conducted a post-replacement RF sweep and latency test across all floors.

symptom: Subscribers traveling along the highway bypass experience persistent high latency and dropped 4G data sessions.
root_cause: Suboptimal handover parameters between adjacent eNodeBs caused ping-pong handovers and dropped packet queues at the cell edge.
resolution: Adjusted the Time-to-Trigger (TTT) and hysteresis parameters for inter-site handovers.
Monitored KPI dashboard for 30 minutes to confirm stabilization.

symptom: Local businesses report erratic 5G standalone (SA) latency performance, fluctuating wildly between 15ms and 500ms.
root_cause: A memory leak in the AMF (Access and Mobility Management Function) virtual network function caused packet processing delays.
resolution: Triggered a graceful failover of the AMF instance to the redundant secondary pod.
Restarted the affected Kubernetes pod and scaled out the deployment replicas.

symptom: Residential zone users experience high latency on 4G networks during peak evening streaming hours.
root_cause: Spectrum resource block exhaustion led to excessive packet scheduling wait times at the MAC layer.
resolution: Activated carrier aggregation (CA) with the 1800MHz and 2600MHz bands to expand the available resource block pool.
Notified performance engineering team to monitor traffic distribution.

symptom: Multiple high-speed rail commuters report dropped 5G NSA data sessions and sudden fallback to 3G while passing through the downtown corridor.
root_cause: Intra-frequency A3 handover event thresholds are set too conservatively, causing the target gNodeB to miss the measurement report before radio link failure occurs due to Doppler shift.
resolution: Adjust the A3 offset (cio) parameter by +2 dB for the affected neighbor cell relations.
Lower the time-to-trigger (TTT) from 64ms to 40ms to accelerate execution.
Monitor KPI trends for handover success rate over the next 24 hours.

symptom: Subscribers inside the new underground shopping mall experience total loss of connectivity when moving from the outdoor macro layer to the indoor DAS.
root_cause: Missing inter-RAT and inter-frequency neighbor relations between the 4G eNodeB macro layer and the neutral host small cell system.
resolution: Update the Automatic Neighbour Relation (ANR) blacklist to force manual integration of missing pci definitions.
Execute an XML bulk configuration push to add the missing X2/Xn interface pairings.
Verify connectivity using a walk-test UE.

symptom: Industrial park users report intermittent call drops and frozen video streams during shift changes when network congestion peaks.
root_cause: Congestion-based mobility load balancing (MLB) is triggering ping-pong handovers between two equally loaded overloaded cells without proper hysteresis.
resolution: Increase the MLB mobility hysteresis timer by 2 seconds to dampen oscillation.
Tune the load threshold parameters to trigger offloading only when traffic exceeds 85% capacity.
Reboot the baseband unit control plane for the primary sector.

symptom: Voice over LTE (VoLTE) calls are abruptly terminating exactly 3 seconds after users cross the boundary between sector 2 and sector 3 of the coastal cell site.
root_cause: S1-based handover preparation failure caused by mismatched QoS profile mappings and GTP-U tunnel establishment timeouts toward the MME.
resolution: Perform a trace on the S1-AP interface to isolate the cause of the Handover Preparation Failure message.
Correct the DSCP markings for QCI 1 bearers on the transmission gateway.
Reset the SCTP association between the eNodeB and the EPC.

symptom: Port authority personnel notice that 5G fixed wireless access routers lose connection every time large cargo ships dock near the pier, causing failed handovers to secondary beams.
root_cause: Severe multipath fading and physical blockage by metal hulls disrupt RSRP measurements, causing the beam failure recovery (BFR) timer to expire before a reliable target beam is found.
resolution: Modify the SSB-based RSRP reporting thresholds to be more tolerant of rapid signal attenuation.
Enable secondary cell group (SCG) failure recovery procedures to speed up radio link failure signaling.
Tilt the antenna downtilt by 1 degree to optimize coverage over the water surface.

symptom: Subscribers driving along the southern highway report ping spikes and data stalls, correlating with frequent RRC Connection Reconfiguration failures during handovers.
root_cause: Physical Cell Identifier (PCI) confusion exists where two neighboring eNodeBs deployed on the same frequency layer share an identical PCI value.
resolution: Re-plan the local PCI matrix to eliminate the collision.
Apply a script to update the PCI assignment on the newly integrated aggressor cell via the Element Management System (EMS).
Clear alarms and verify handover success rate counters.

symptom: Residential users complain of slow page loads and intermittent disconnects when moving rooms, traced back to failed intra-site handovers between 2.6GHz and 1.8GHz layers.
root_cause: Layer 3 mobility rules favor the higher frequency band prematurely, causing radio link failure before the UE can successfully process the measurement control command.
resolution: Adjust the A2 measurement report trigger threshold for inter-frequency handovers down by 4 dBm.
Update the priority settings in the System Information Block Type 5 (SIB5) to prioritize the 1.8GHz layer for deep indoor coverage.
Perform a drive test validation.

symptom: University campus users experience complete loss of data service during peak lecture change times when transitioning from outdoor 5G coverage to auditorium small cells.
root_cause: The Xn interface between the macro gNodeB and the indoor integrated access point experienced a transport layer path failure due to a BGP route flap.
resolution: Coordinate with the IP core team to stabilize the OSPF/BGP routing table across the campus backhaul network.
Restart the IPSec tunnel endpoints on both communicating nodes.
Verify Xn-C and Xn-U path availability via OAM ping utilities.

symptom: Commercial delivery drivers report that their handheld scanners fail to maintain sessions when moving between blocks in the old city center, resulting in frequent 'Handover Time Out' events.
root_cause: High building penetration loss causes the timing advance (TA) value to drift out of range, rendering the random access channel (RACH)-less handover procedure invalid.
resolution: Configure dedicated preamble allocations for contention-free handovers on critical target cells.
Increase the handover command guard timer from 100ms to 200ms.
Retest data session continuity with a field diagnostic tool.

symptom: Emergency services deployed in the industrial zone report intermittent loss of priority data streams during mobility scenarios due to unexpected bearer dropouts.
root_cause: The target eNodeB rejected the handover request because of insufficient admission control resources for high-priority ARP (Allocation and Retention Priority) bearers.
resolution: Reconfigure the admission control preemption parameters to guarantee resource reservation for emergency QCI profiles.
Increase the maximum permitted active bearer count on the target cell baseband card.
Run a simulated handover test for priority classes.

symptom: Customer reports total loss of internet connection and the LOS LED on the Huawei ONT is flashing red. No changes were made to the home network setup.
root_cause: The drop fiber cable was inadvertently severed by landscaping crew working near the property boundary, resulting in complete signal attenuation.
resolution: Dispatched field technician to splice the broken drop cable and tested light levels to ensure optimal RX power of -21 dBm.

symptom: NOC monitoring flagged an offline ONT at a residential address. Customer states the device power light is on, but the PON light remains completely unlit.
root_cause: The SC/APC connector at the optical wall outlet became loose, causing the optical signal to fail the transceiver handshake.
resolution: Instructed customer over the phone to securely reseat the fiber jumper into the optical wall outlet and rebooted the ONT remotely.

symptom: Subscriber experiences intermittent connection drops over the last 48 hours, culminating in a permanent blinking PON light this morning.
root_cause: Micro-bends in the internal micro-duct caused by heavy furniture placement gradually degraded the fiber until total attenuation occurred.
resolution: Rerouted the internal fiber run along the baseboard away from pinch points and replaced the damaged jumper cable.

symptom: Multiple subscribers in the same apartment building report simultaneous loss of FTTH service with blinking LOS indicators on their ONTs.
root_cause: A rodent chewed through the multi-dwelling unit (MDU) riser cable inside the basement telecom closet.
resolution: Replaced the damaged section of the MDU riser cable and installed protective armored conduits around exposed fiber runs.

symptom: Customer's Nokia ONT shows a steady power light, but the PON indicator is slowly flashing, indicating it is ranging but failing to register.
root_cause: The ONT's GPON Serial Number (ONU SN) was de-provisioned during a recent database migration script error on the OLT.
resolution: Re-added the correct ONU SN and provisioning profile to the parent OLT interface via the EMS CLI.

symptom: New installation ticket where the technician could not complete activation because the ZTE ONT fails to sync with the OLT port.
root_cause: The port on the feeder splitter in the street cabinet was incorrectly patched to an inactive OLT card during construction.
resolution: Traced the circuit layout, moved the patch cord to the designated active OLT port in the splitter cabinet, and verified successful registration.

symptom: Customer reports no internet access after a severe lightning storm last night. The ONT has all lights off despite being plugged into a working outlet.
root_cause: A power surge traveled through the power adapter, frying the internal power management IC of the ONT and rendering it dead.
resolution: Replaced the fried ONT unit with a new hardware revision, updated the firmware, and provisioned it on the active OLT.

symptom: Subscriber complains that the PON LED has been flashing green continuously for hours without establishing a stable broadband link.
root_cause: Dirty fiber end-face on the patch cord connector causing high optical return loss (ORL) and preventing successful ranging.
resolution: Cleaned the optical connector using a One-Click cleaner and verified clean inspection scope results before reconnecting.

symptom: NOC alerts show a sudden drop of 32 ONTs on a specific GPON tree going into a persistent LOS state.
root_cause: Municipal roadworks caused an accidental fiber cut on the primary feeder cable leaving the central office hub.
resolution: Noticed splice team deployed to the excavation site, performed emergency fusion splicing of the 144-count feeder cable, and confirmed all ONTs recovered.

symptom: User reports that the ONT LOS light is red and service has been down since morning after a local utility pole maintenance.
root_cause: Utility workers inadvertently unhooked and pinched the aerial drop cable while restringing power lines.
resolution: Sent aerial drop repair crew to re-tension the span, clear the pinch hazard, and re-anchor the drop clamp securely.

symptom: Customer reports total loss of internet connection and the LOS LED on the Huawei ONT is flashing red continuously.
root_cause: Physical break in the drop fiber cable caused by landscaping work near the property boundary, resulting in zero optical power at the receiver.
resolution: Dispatched field technician to splice and repair the damaged drop fiber. Tested optical power levels to ensure they are within the -18dBm to -24dBm operational range.

symptom: NOC alarm indicates multiple ONTs offline on GPON port 3. Customers in the building report sudden loss of sync.
root_cause: A faulty patch cord inside the local PoP split the optical signal, and a loose connector at the 1:32 optical splitter caused severe attenuation for the entire branch.
resolution: Re-seated the SC/APC connector at the secondary optical splitter and replaced the damaged jumper cable. Verified all ONTs on the port re-synchronized successfully.

symptom: Subscriber states the PON LED is blinking green indefinitely and the broadband service is completely down.
root_cause: The ONT's serial number (GPON SN/Password) was inadvertently unassigned from the OLT profile during a recent database migration.
resolution: Re-provisioned the subscriber's ONT serial number on the Huawei OLT using the correct provisioning template and forced a re-registration cycle.

symptom: Customer intermittent connection dropping to a flashing LOS light every afternoon, followed by complete sync loss.
root_cause: Micro-bend in the indoor fiber optic cable due to heavy furniture pressing against the fiber wall outlet, exacerbated by thermal expansion.
resolution: Relocated the optical wall outlet and replaced the compromised internal fiber jumper with a armored patch cable. Confirmed stable light levels.

symptom: ONT power LED is on, but PON light remains dark with no link activity. Customer rebooted multiple times with no change.
root_cause: Internal transceiver failure within the Nokia ONT hardware, causing it to fail the optical handshake with the OLT.
resolution: Dispatched a replacement unit to the subscriber premises. Swapped out the defective ONT, registered the new MAC/GPON SN on the ACS server, and tested speeds.

symptom: NOC alerts show an isolated ONT with dying gasp alarm followed by permanent LOS status.
root_cause: Accidental unplugging of the power supply unit by the customer while cleaning, combined with a dirty optical connector upon plugging back in.
resolution: Instructed customer to secure the power connection. Cleaned the ONT optical port with an One-Click cleaner to remove dust contamination and restored optical link.

symptom: Subscriber experiences complete loss of service after a severe thunderstorm. PON light is flashing slowly.
root_cause: Power surge through the aerial drop cable induced a fault in the ONT's optical receiver module, preventing proper synchronization with the OLT.
resolution: Replaced the fried ONT unit with a surge-protected model and installed an external fiber optic lightning protection grounding block on the exterior wall.

symptom: Multiple customer complaints of 'No Internet' and blinking PON LEDs across a newly deployed residential sub-division.
root_cause: The feeder fiber connected to the distribution node suffered high macro-bending due to poor tensioning during aerial deployment by the contractor.
resolution: Notified the outside plant contractor to re-tension the aerial fiber span. Inspected the affected pole line and verified optical return loss improved to acceptable standards.

symptom: Customer reports that the ONT LOS LED turns solid red whenever it rains heavily.
root_cause: Water ingress inside the aerial fiber closure splice tray caused microscopic water freezing/expansion, creating high optical attenuation during wet weather.
resolution: Resealed the watertight aerial splice closure, cleaned the affected splice cassettes, and replaced two fusion splices that showed high insertion loss.

symptom: Subscriber ONT fails to authenticate after firmware auto-update, showing a solid LOS and flashing internet light.
root_cause: Firmware mismatch caused the ONT's TR-069 configuration parameters to corrupt, dropping the VLAN tagging required for OLT communication.
resolution: Pushed a factory reset command via the ACS server and reapplied the baseline TR-069 configuration file. Verified successful OLT registration and IP lease.

symptom: VoIP calls are experiencing severe jitter and one-way audio during peak business hours between the branch and HQ.
root_cause: The WAN interface egress policy was missing a priority queue assignment for DSCP EF traffic, causing voice packets to be dropped during congestion.
resolution: 1. Updated the MQC policy-map to allocate dedicated bandwidth and priority queuing to DSCP EF traffic. 2. Applied the updated policy to the WAN interface egress direction. 3. Verified jitter levels dropped below 15ms under load.

symptom: Enterprise resource planning (ERP) application syncs are timing out intermittently despite normal link utilization.
root_cause: Misconfigured traffic policer on the core switch was improperly dropping TCP ACK packets due to an overly aggressive burst size calculation.
resolution: 1. Adjusted the committed burst (Bc) and excess burst (Be) parameters on the class-based policer for the ERP traffic class. 2. Monitored interface drop counters to ensure TCP ACKs pass without artificial packet loss.

symptom: Real-time video conferencing streams are freezing and showing high packet loss across the inter-site transport link.
root_cause: Video traffic was incorrectly mapped to the default best-effort queue instead of the designated AF41 scavenger/multimedia priority queue.
resolution: 1. Modified the access-list and class-map definitions to correctly identify video conferencing UDP port ranges. 2. Re-bound the class-map to the correct priority queue in the transport policy-map.

symptom: Batch file backups running overnight are saturating the access link, causing critical payment gateway transactions to fail.
root_cause: Lack of outbound shaping on the transport interface allowed bulk backup traffic to starve latency-sensitive database replication traffic.
resolution: 1. Configured hierarchical shaping on the sub-interface to cap maximum egress bandwidth at the contracted SLA rate. 2. Implemented weighted fair queuing (WFQ) to guarantee minimum bandwidth percentages for the payment application.

symptom: Branch office users report that web browsing is extremely sluggish while file transfers run smoothly.
root_cause: A recent configuration template push inverted the bandwidth weights, giving scavenger traffic a higher bandwidth guarantee than standard business web traffic.
resolution: 1. Reviewed the active policy-map configuration via CLI. 2. Reassigned correct bandwidth-remaining percentages to standard TCP web traffic classes and demoted peer-to-peer/scavenger classes.

symptom: Remote desktop (RDP) sessions are lagging heavily when multiple employees access the terminal server simultaneously.
root_cause: DSCP-to-COS re-marking was misconfigured at the layer 2 boundary, causing RDP packets to lose their priority marking when crossing the transport switch.
resolution: 1. Fixed the layer 2 trust state on the access switch ports to 'trust dscp'. 2. Corrected the policy map mapping table to ensure incoming DSCP 32 is properly mapped to CoS 5.

symptom: Critical SCADA telemetry data packets are arriving out of order and suffering from high latency spikes.
root_cause: Low-latency queue (LLQ) was configured without a strict bandwidth limit, leading to queue starvation for other essential management protocols during bursts.
resolution: 1. Assigned a strict explicit bandwidth limit of 1Gbps to the LLQ class. 2. Enabled random early detection (WRED) on the default queue to smooth out TCP traffic bursts.

symptom: Guest Wi-Fi users are consuming all available transport bandwidth, impacting internal corporate SaaS applications.
root_cause: Rate-limiting policy on the guest VLAN interface was not applied correctly, bypassing the egress shaping mechanism.
resolution: 1. Applied an ingress rate-limit policy on the guest switch port VLAN interface. 2. Verified that guest traffic is capped at the designated threshold and internal apps receive guaranteed bandwidth.

symptom: Financial trading platform connection drops intermittently during high market volatility periods.
root_cause: Tail drop was occurring prematurely on the queue because WRED thresholds were set too low for high-throughput financial data streams.
resolution: 1. Adjusted the WRED drop thresholds upward to accommodate larger burst profiles for the specific traffic class. 2. Confirmed packet drop counters ceased incrementing under load.

symptom: IP Telephony endpoints are failing SIP registration and dropping calls during routine network traffic spikes.
root_cause: Control plane policing (CoPP) policy misclassification was dropping SIP signaling packets (UDP port 5060) as unauthorized traffic.
resolution: 1. Updated the CoPP access-list to explicitly permit SIP and RTP control traffic with high-priority classification. 2. Applied the updated policy to the route processor and tested registration stability.

symptom: Users at the Tunis-01 office are unable to resolve external domain names, resulting in complete internet access failure.
root_cause: The primary internal DNS forwarders crashed due to a memory leak, and backup forwarders were misconfigured in the DHCP scope.
resolution: Restarted the Bind9 DNS service on the primary name server and updated the forwarder IP addresses in the core DHCP configuration.

symptom: Applications in Sfax-01 cannot communicate with internal microservices, throwing 'Name or service not known' exceptions.
root_cause: An expired SSL certificate on the authoritative local DNS appliance caused replication to halt and corrupted the local zone database.
resolution: Renewed the appliance certificate, forced a manual zone transfer from the primary DNS master, and verified service health.

symptom: External clients report that the corporate web portal hosted in Sousse-01 is intermittently unreachable via domain name.
root_cause: The TTL on the apex A record was set too low during a migration, and upstream ISP caching servers experienced intermittent packet loss.
resolution: Increased the A record TTL to 3600 seconds and flushed the authoritative DNS cache to stabilize external lookups.

symptom: Branch office users at Bizerte-01 are experiencing extremely slow page load times and frequent DNS timeout errors.
root_cause: Local workstations were hardcoded with public DNS resolvers that were being throttled by the local firewall's rate-limiting rules.
resolution: Pushed a group policy update redirecting all DNS queries to the secure internal caching resolvers located at the site.

symptom: All DNS resolution for the internal domain '.corp.local' has failed entirely across the Gabes-01 campus network.
root_cause: A recent firewall rule update blocked UDP and TCP port 53 traffic between the internal VLANs and the local Active Directory DNS controllers.
resolution: Modified the firewall ACLs to explicitly allow bi-directional DNS traffic on port 53 for all internal subnet ranges.

symptom: The Nabeul-01 site monitoring system is alerting that internal servers cannot resolve names of newly provisioned cloud resources.
root_cause: Conditional forwarders for the cloud provider's private DNS zone were accidentally deleted during a routine network cleanup script.
resolution: Re-added the conditional forwarder entries pointing to the cloud provider's DNS endpoints and tested resolution using nslookup.

symptom: Kairouan-01 users report that specific partner websites are not loading, while general internet browsing works fine.
root_cause: DNSSEC validation failure occurred due to a clock skew of over 5 minutes on the local caching nameserver.
resolution: Synchronized the local server's system time with the corporate NTP pool and restarted the DNS validation service.

symptom: Critical database cluster in Tunis-02 suffered a split-brain event because nodes could not resolve each other's hostnames.
root_cause: A syntax error introduced in the local zone file during a manual IP re-allocation caused the entire zone to fail loading upon service restart.
resolution: Corrected the trailing dot syntax error in the zone file, validated the configuration using named-checkzone, and reloaded the zone.

symptom: Employees at Sfax-01 attempting to connect via VPN are failing authentication due to DNS lookup failures for the RADIUS server.
root_cause: The split-tunnel DNS configuration on the VPN gateway omitted the internal search suffix, causing external resolution attempts to fail.
resolution: Updated the VPN profile configuration on the gateway to include the correct internal DNS search suffixes and pushed updates to clients.

symptom: Nabeul-01 office experiences intermittent name resolution failures for external domains every afternoon during peak hours.
root_cause: The local DNS server reached its maximum concurrent query limit due to a localized malware beaconing loop from a compromised workstation.
resolution: Identified and isolated the compromised host via EDR, increased the DNS server's worker thread allocation, and cleared the resolver cache.

symptom: VoIP calls are experiencing severe jitter and one-way audio during peak business hours between headquarters and the branch office.
root_cause: The WAN interface egress policy queue for real-time voice traffic was misconfigured with an incorrect bandwidth ceiling, causing voice packets to drop during bursts.
resolution: Access the core edge router and locate the QoS policy-map.
Adjust the priority queue bandwidth allocation for voice traffic from 5% to 20%.
Apply the updated policy to the WAN interface and monitor drop rates using 'show policy-map interface'.

symptom: Critical database replication traffic is timing out intermittently, while non-critical bulk file transfers are performing without issue.
root_cause: A recent configuration push incorrectly classified database replication traffic into the 'best-effort' queue instead of the designated mission-critical class.
resolution: Update the Access Control List (ACL) matching the database replication ports.
Re-map the traffic class to the expedited forwarding (EF) DSCP value of 46.
Verify packet marking using packet captures and verify replication stability.

symptom: Video conferencing feeds are freezing and dropping frames across the regional office network.
root_cause: The hierarchical QoS (H-QoS) parent policy on the provider-edge handoff was set to a shaper rate lower than the contracted CIR, starving the video queue.
resolution: Modify the parent shaper rate on the WAN interface to match the exact Committed Information Rate provided by the ISP.
Validate the child policy queues for video and ensure proper buffer allocation.
Conduct a test video conference to confirm frame rate stability.

symptom: Branch users report that internal web applications are sluggish, despite link utilization sitting below 40%.
root_cause: Default class-map matching was catching all TCP traffic indiscriminately, overriding the custom classification rules meant to prioritize enterprise SaaS traffic.
resolution: Reorder the class-map sequence in the modular QoS CLI (MQC) policy to evaluate specific enterprise apps before the default catch-all class.
Commit the configuration changes and clear interface counters.
Perform a latency and response time check on the target web applications.

symptom: Backup jobs running over the transport network are consuming 100% of the available link bandwidth, causing total packet loss for other services.
root_cause: The transport layer traffic policer was disabled during maintenance, allowing backup traffic to bypass bandwidth limits without rate-limiting or shaping.
resolution: Re-enable the traffic policer on the backup VLAN interface.
Configure a strict bandwidth ceiling of 30% for the backup class-map during daytime hours.
Monitor interface utilization graphs to ensure normal traffic is no longer impacted.

symptom: POS (Point of Sale) terminal transactions are timing out intermittently during heavy network loads.
root_cause: POS traffic DSCP markings were being trusted by the access switch, but the upstream transport router was set to 'no ip qos trust', remarking all packets to DSCP 0.
resolution: Configure 'ip qos trust dscp' on the transport router ingress interface facing the access switch.
Verify that the policy-map correctly prioritizes DSCP 34 (AF41) used by the POS terminals.
Run a transaction test script to verify zero timeouts.

symptom: IP-based security camera streams are heavily pixelated and dropping packets across the campus transport link.
root_cause: Random Early Detection (WRED) drop thresholds were set too aggressively on the video queue, dropping packets prematurely before congestion actually occurred.
resolution: Access the switch interface configuration and modify the WRED profile parameters.
Increase the queue-limit and adjust the minimum/maximum threshold percentages for the video traffic class.
Verify stream quality via the security management platform.

symptom: Remote desktop (RDP) sessions from the field office are excessively laggy and unresponsive.
root_cause: Interactive traffic was incorrectly mapped to the scavenger DSCP value (CS1) instead of the interactive/control DSCP value (CS2/AF31).
resolution: Update the port-based classification ACL to correctly tag TCP port 3389 traffic with DSCP 26.
Re-apply the policy-map to the transport interface.
Test an active RDP session to confirm improved responsiveness.

symptom: VoIP and critical ERP traffic are experiencing identical degradation during bandwidth spikes, indicating lack of prioritization.
root_cause: The transport interface queue-limit was exhausted because Tail Drop was active instead of Weighted Fair Queuing (WFQ), causing FIFO drops across all classes.
resolution: Enable fair-queue within the custom policy-map class definitions on the WAN router.
Allocate guaranteed minimum bandwidth percentages explicitly for VoIP and ERP classes.
Check buffer drop counters to ensure strict priority queueing is functioning correctly.

symptom: Network monitoring alerts indicate high latency on non-critical bulk data transfers, but customer reports no operational impact.
root_cause: A typo in the bandwidth allocation statement left 50% of the link unassigned, causing the scheduler to mismanage leftover bandwidth distribution.
resolution: Review the running policy-map configuration for syntax and allocation summing errors.
Adjust the 'bandwidth remaining percent' statements so that all classes total 100%.
Save the configuration and verify queue statistics.

symptom: Multiple 5G standalone users in the downtown area are experiencing immediate attach rejects with cause code #15 (No suitable cells in tracking area).
root_cause: A recent MME/AMF configuration script omitted the new tracking area code (TAC) expansion from the neighboring gNodeB neighbor relation tables.
resolution: Updated the AMF configuration via the OSS-RC to include the missing TACs in the tracking area list and pushed a synchronization command to the affected gNodeBs.

symptom: Subscribers attempting to attach to the newly deployed 4G sector are receiving 'EPS authentication unacceptable' rejects, causing persistent connection loops.
root_cause: A mismatch in the security anchor key derivation function (KDF) parameters between the upgraded eNodeB and the legacy HSS interface.
resolution: Re-aligned the cryptographic algorithm profiles on the local security gateway and restarted the eNodeB control plane process.

symptom: IoT devices using narrowband 4G report intermittent attach failures with cause #7 (EPS services not allowed).
root_cause: The HSS subscriber database contained outdated subscription profiles where the APN for NB-IoT was inadvertently disabled during a bulk profile migration.
resolution: Restored the active APN subscription profiles for the affected IMSI ranges via the Unified Data Management (UDM) provisioning tool.

symptom: Roaming 5G NSA users are locked out of the network, encountering continuous attach rejects referencing 'PLMN not allowed'.
root_cause: An expired roaming agreement update file left out the specific PLMN ID in the VPLMN routing table on the local STP.
resolution: Manually ingested the updated GSMA PR9.6 routing tables into the Signal Transfer Point and verified diameter routing connectivity.

symptom: Field engineers testing a new 5G small cell notice that all initial registration requests are rejected with cause #11 (PLMN not allowed).
root_cause: The PLMN ID broadcasted in the SIB1 message of the small cell was incorrectly set to a test operator ID instead of the production PLMN.
resolution: Connected to the small cell local WebGUI, corrected the PLMN ID configuration, and performed a soft reboot of the radio unit.

symptom: High volume of 4G attach rejects with cause #3 (Illegal UE) reported by customers using imported smartphone models.
root_cause: The EIR (Equipment Identity Register) blacklist database erroneously flagged a newly allocated block of IMEI numbers as stolen.
resolution: Whitelisted the affected IMEI TAC prefix range in the EIR and cleared the local authentication cache on the MME pool.

symptom: Subscribers crossing the regional border experience sudden drop-offs and subsequent attach rejects with cause #27 (N1 mode not allowed).
root_cause: The inter-RAT handover parameters on the source eNodeB incorrectly signaled 5G core capabilities to devices without active dual-connectivity licenses.
resolution: Modified the mobility control parameters in the eNodeB CLI to correctly filter N1 mode capabilities based on active subscriber profiles.

symptom: Emergency backup terminals fail to attach to the LTE network, returning cause #19 (ESM failure).
root_cause: Resource exhaustion on the local PGW led to a failure in allocating default Bearer IP addresses during the attach procedure.
resolution: Restarted the local PGW control plane blade to release hung session states and expanded the dynamic IP pool allocation.

symptom: Users report sporadic 5G attach rejects accompanied by a long signaling delay before the failure message appears.
root_cause: Severe packet jitter and packet loss on the fronthaul transport link caused timeouts during the NAS security mode complete phase.
resolution: Dispatched a technician to replace a degraded SFP+ transceiver on the transport switch and verified optical power levels.

symptom: A subset of 4G enterprise routers fail to re-attach after a scheduled site power cycle, throwing cause #14 (EPS services and non-EPS services not allowed).
root_cause: The MME pool experienced a split-brain condition where stale context data prevented the re-registration of static-IP machine-type communications (MTC) devices.
resolution: Purged the orphaned subscriber contexts from the active MME database and forced a localized tracking area update (TAU) broadcast.

symptom: NOC dashboard alerts indicate a sudden surge in Mobility Management Entity (MME) CPU utilization exceeding 92% in the central region, accompanied by high signalling delay for attaching users.
root_cause: A localized flash crowd event at a stadium caused a massive spike in simultaneous Tracking Area Update (TAU) and attach requests, overwhelming the MME control plane processing queues.
resolution:
1. Activated local overload control algorithms and dropped low-priority device signalling.
2. Rerouted incoming excess signalling traffic to secondary standby MME pools.
3. Monitored CPU recovery to nominal operational thresholds.

symptom: Subscribers in the downtown district are experiencing frequent 5G-to-4G fallback and intermittent data session drops during peak evening hours.
root_cause: 5G Standalone (5SA) Access and Mobility Management Function (AMF) experienced thread starvation due to an exponential increase in PDU session establishment requests.
resolution:
1. Scaled up AMF microservice pod replicas in the container orchestration platform.
2. Adjusted admission control thresholds for non-critical IoT devices.
3. Verified stabilization of session setup success rates.

symptom: Customer care reports an influx of complaints regarding slow browsing speeds and inability to stream video over the 4G network across the industrial zone.
root_cause: The Serving Gateway (SGW) data plane throughput reached 98% capacity, causing packet buffering delays and high latency across multiple eNodeBs.
resolution:
1. Initiated load balancing policies to offload data traffic to an adjacent SGW.
2. Dispatched a request to the engineering team for permanent capacity expansion of the user plane interface.

symptom: Automated alarms report high memory consumption on the HTTP/2 Proxy (SEPP/SCP) handling roaming traffic, resulting in rejected incoming session requests.
root_cause: A signaling storm caused by a roaming partner looping registration requests flooded the Service Communication Proxy (SCP), exhausting available heap memory.
resolution:
1. Implemented rate-limiting rules on the border gateway for the offending partner PLMN.
2. Restarted the affected SCP pods to clear stale memory allocations.
3. Notified the external roaming partner's NOC.

symptom: Field engineers note that 5G Home Broadband users are intermittently losing internet connectivity with error code 'NAS cause #22: congestion'.
root_cause: The Session Management Function (SMF) hit maximum concurrent session limits during a regional fiber outage that forced fixed-wireless access points onto the cellular core.
resolution:
1. Temporarily increased the maximum concurrent session limit in the SMF configuration profile.
2. Applied QoS throttling to heavy background download profiles to free up resources.

symptom: NOC monitoring shows a high failure rate for Voice over LTE (VoLTE) call setups, with the Proxy-Call Session Control Function (P-CSCF) reporting resource exhaustion.
root_cause: A localized flash crowd triggered a massive volume of simultaneous SIP INVITE messages, overwhelming the IMS core signaling processors.
resolution:
1. Enabled SIP overload control (RFC 7339) on the P-CSCF.
2. Scaled out additional IMS application server instances via the MANO orchestrator.
3. Confirmed drop in call setup failure rates.

symptom: Users report sudden disconnection from data services along the coastal highway corridor, with gNodeBs dropping active Radio Resource Control (RRC) connections.
root_cause: The User Plane Function (UPF) experienced memory buffer exhaustion due to an unoptimized TCP window size configuration by a major content provider.
resolution:
1. Cleared hung TCP sessions via the UPF CLI.
2. Imposed temporary rate-shaping policies on top autonomous system numbers causing the buffer bloat.

symptom: Alarms indicate Home Subscriber Server (HSS) database query response times exceeding 3000ms, delaying user authentication procedures.
root_cause: A malfunctioning enterprise IoT application repeatedly hammered the HSS with authentication requests due to an aggressive retry storm.
resolution:
1. Blocked the offending enterprise APN IP range at the firewall level.
2. Flushed the HSS transaction logs and optimized database query execution plans.
3. Contacted the enterprise customer regarding their retry logic.

symptom: Subscribers attempting to attach to the network receive 'Service Option Not Supported' messages during a regional event.
root_cause: The Diameter Routing Agent (DRA) saturated its processing capacity routing AAA requests between the EPC and the subscriber database, causing widespread timeout drops.
resolution:
1. Redirected excess Diameter traffic over secondary routing paths.
2. Temporarily disabled non-essential telemetry logging to free up CPU cycles on the DRA cluster.

symptom: NOC receives alerts of escalating CPU temperatures and high load averages on the Policy and Charging Rules Function (PCRF) cluster.
root_cause: A sudden burst of heavy video streaming across thousands of subscribers triggered continuous dynamic policy recalculations, starving PCRF worker threads.
resolution:
1. Offloaded static subscriber policy profiles to local cache memory.
2. Temporarily suspended real-time bandwidth quota re-evaluations for pre-paid profiles during the peak window.

symptom: Customers in the northern region are reporting intermittent connectivity to international destinations, with traceroutes showing traffic looping through an unexpected third-party transit provider.
root_cause: An upstream peer accidentally advertised a more specific /23 prefix for our primary IP block, causing global BGP path hijacking.
resolution: Contacted the peer to withdraw the faulty advertisement, applied strict AS-path filtering on our edge routers, and cleared the BGP session.

symptom: Monitoring alerts show a massive spike in outbound traffic volume and packet loss towards specific Asian cloud endpoints originating from the core gateway.
root_cause: A downstream customer misconfigured their routing policies, leaking our full internal routing table out to the public internet.

symptom: Internal applications hosted at the data center are experiencing elevated latency and asymmetric routing patterns observed via edge telemetry.
root_cause: A lateral peering partner leaked routes from another Tier-1 network, making a suboptimal path appear as the best AS-path.

symptom: The NOC dashboard flagged a sudden drop in aggregate bandwidth utilization accompanied by unreachable destination alerts for several enterprise VPN endpoints.
root_cause: Accidental prefix re-origination by a partner ISP resulted in a route leak that hijacked traffic destined for our corporate VPN gateways.

symptom: Branch offices are reporting complete blackholing of specific public subnets, while internal site-to-site tunnels remain fully operational.
root_cause: An invalid BGP community tag stripped by a transit provider propagated an internal route leak across multiple exchange points.
resolution: Updated route-map policies to drop routes lacking required origin AS tags and reset the BGP adjacency with the transit provider.

symptom: External API consumers are experiencing connection timeouts, and looking glass servers show our prefixes being advertised with an incorrect next-hop IP.
root_cause: A misconfigured prefix-list on the border router allowed private customer routes to leak into the global BGP routing table.
resolution: Corrected the prefix-list parameters on the outbound route policy and executed a soft reconfiguration inbound/outbound.

symptom: Degraded voice-over-IP quality and jitter spikes reported by users, coinciding with sudden routing flaps on the primary edge interface.
root_cause: A route leak from an adjacent autonomous system introduced a suboptimal transit path with excessive latency.
resolution: Implemented Max-Prefix limits on the peer session and adjusted local preference values to prefer our direct transit links.

symptom: Complete isolation of a specific service subnet; external users receive 'No Route to Host' errors despite firewall rules being correct.
root_cause: An upstream provider suffered a partial route leak, overwriting our valid static BGP announcements with dead-end paths.
resolution: Notified the upstream NOC of the anomaly, established an emergency static route override, and monitored BGP convergence.

symptom: Network operations center received multiple alerts regarding unusual traffic patterns flowing through an unexpected international transit link.
root_cause: A secondary transit provider accepted and re-advertised our internal management prefixes due to missing out-bound filter filters.
resolution: Applied explicit prefix-filtering filters blocking internal address spaces at the provider boundary and bounced the BGP peer.

symptom: Clients connected to the regional PoP are unable to resolve or reach specific partner networks, resulting in failed transaction processing.
root_cause: A cascading BGP route leak from an Internet Exchange Point (IXP) peer flooded our edge routers with invalid path selections.
resolution: Temporarily disabled the affected IXP peering session, enforced RPKI validation checks, and restored the session cleanly.

symptom: Multiple users reporting zero 5G indoor coverage and frequent dropouts inside the main shopping mall during peak hours.
root_cause: The local 3.5GHz Massive MIMO active antenna unit experienced a partial RF module failure, degrading sector 2 output power.
resolution: Dispatched field technicians to replace the faulty Remote Radio Unit (RRU) and re-flashed the firmware to restore full transmission power.

symptom: Subscribers traveling along the southern highway corridor experience sudden loss of 4G data connectivity and fallback to 2G.
root_cause: An overlapping coverage hole was created following an accidental azimuth tilt adjustment on eNodeB sector 3 during routine maintenance.
resolution: Performed remote antenna tilt optimization via the EMS to restore proper overlap and continuous radio coverage along the highway.

symptom: Residential customers complain of extremely slow 4G speeds and high packet loss inside their apartments throughout the afternoon.
root_cause: Severe inter-cell interference caused by an uncoordinated PCI (Physical Cell Identity) collision between neighboring micro-cells.
