resolution: Executed an automated PCI re-planning script across the cluster via the SON (Self-Organizing Networks) server to eliminate signal collision.

symptom: Complete outage of 5G Standalone (SA) service in the central business district, forcing devices onto congested 4G bands.
root_cause: The gNodeB lost synchronization with the primary Grandmaster clock, causing the TDD (Time Division Duplexing) frame alignment to fail.
resolution: Reset the PTP (Precision Time Protocol) grandmaster interface configuration on the backhaul router and verified phase sync lock.

symptom: Industrial park tenants report intermittent 4G signal drops and inability to maintain stable IoT device connections.
root_cause: Heavy foliage growth around the tower site severely attenuated the lower-band 800MHz propagation path.
resolution: Authorized an emergency tree-trimming crew to clear the Fresnel zone obstruction directly in front of sector 1.

symptom: Beachfront visitors experience poor 4G/5G throughput and dropped voice calls despite full signal indicator bars.
root_cause: Massive seasonal subscriber influx caused severe resource block exhaustion on the primary 1800MHz frequency layer.
resolution: Activated cell-splitting parameters and enabled load balancing to offload excess traffic onto the adjacent 2100MHz carrier layer.

symptom: University campus users report weak 5G indoor coverage inside the newly constructed concrete library building.
root_cause: High-emissivity Low-E glass installed on the new building blocked high-frequency 3.5GHz signals from penetrating the indoor environment.
resolution: Designed and deployed a dedicated indoor Distributed Antenna System (DAS) connected to the donor macro site.

symptom: Port authority operations report degraded 4G telemetry coverage along the outer container docks and loading bays.
root_cause: High-capacity metal shipping container stacks shifted position, creating a massive RF shadow that blocked line-of-sight propagation.
resolution: Installed a supplementary outdoor repeater unit on a nearby light mast to fill the shadow zone created by the container stacks.

symptom: Subscribers in the historic medina district experience sudden degradation in 4G data rates and high RRC connection failure rates.
root_cause: A lightning strike induced a power surge that damaged the tower's tower-mounted amplifier (TMA), drastically degrading receiver sensitivity.
resolution: Replaced the damaged TMA unit and tested VSWR (Voltage Standing Wave Ratio) values to ensure optimal feeder cable performance.

symptom: Commuters report erratic 5G coverage switching rapidly between 4G and 5G with frequent data stalls near the central transport hub.
root_cause: Misconfigured handover hysteresis parameters between the 5G gNodeB and 4G eNodeB caused continuous ping-pong handovers.
resolution: Tuned the A2/A5 handover threshold parameters in the OSS-RC to stabilize mobility and eliminate unnecessary radio state transitions.

symptom: Customer reports complete loss of internet service on their FTTH line. PON LED is green and steady, but the ONT fails to obtain an IP address via DHCP.
root_cause: The OLT profile was incorrectly configured with default VLAN 10 instead of the subscriber's assigned enterprise VLAN 200 during automated provisioning.
resolution: 1. Access the OLT management interface and locate the subscriber's ONU port. 2. Remove the incorrect VLAN configuration and rebind the port to VLAN 200. 3. Force an ONU reboot and verify DHCP lease acquisition.

symptom: Subscriber states that IPTV service is working, but broadband internet is completely dead. Router is stuck at 'WAN port is unplugged or authenticating' state.
root_cause: Service profile mapping error in the AAA/RADIUS integration caused the internet traffic to be tagged with the IPTV VLAN ID 100 instead of internet VLAN 50.
resolution: 1. Update the subscriber service profile in the provisioning system to map data traffic to VLAN 50. 2. Push the updated configuration to the access switch. 3. Instruct the customer to power cycle their residential gateway.

symptom: NOC alarm triggered for a newly activated GPON zone where multiple ONTs are registering successfully on the physical layer, but dropping authentication packets completely.
root_cause: A manual trunk port configuration change on the aggregation switch omitted the specific customer VLAN 312 required for the new housing development.
resolution: 1. Log into the aggregation switch CLI. 2. Add VLAN 312 to the uplink trunk interface connecting to the BRAS. 3. Verify mac-address learning on the interface.

symptom: Business customer complains that their dedicated static IP block is unreachable and VPN tunnels are down. Basic fiber link check shows optical power is optimal (-19 dBm).
root_cause: During a database migration, the customer's CPE port was accidentally mapped to the residential VLAN pool (VLAN 10) instead of the Metro-Ethernet corporate VLAN 850.
resolution: 1. Correct the VLAN assignment in the OSS database from VLAN 10 to VLAN 850. 2. Apply the configuration template to theolt-agg-02 device. 3. Verify end-to-end ping response to the customer gateway.

symptom: User experiences extremely high packet loss and latency spikes when attempting to access local streaming servers. Web browsing works intermittently.
root_cause: Double-tagging (QinQ) misconfiguration caused the outer VLAN tag to mismatch with the Metro-Ethernet provider network transport VLAN 402.
resolution: 1. Inspect the service-port parameters on the OLT using CLI. 2. Modify the QinQ inner/outer VLAN mapping to correctly reflect VLAN 402. 3. Run a baseline ping test to confirm packet loss is resolved.

symptom: New FTTH activation fails during the field technician's final test. The ONT online light is blinking and fails to establish a session with the localBRAS.
root_cause: Typo in the field work order entry resulted in the service being provisioned on VLAN 77 instead of the correct regional administrative VLAN 71.
resolution: 1. Coordinate with the field technician to confirm the correct work order details. 2. Re-provision the ONU interface on the OLT with VLAN 71. 3. Wait for ONT re-registration and confirm active PPPoE session.

symptom: Multiple subscribers in the same apartment building report sudden service disconnection simultaneously. Physical fiber inspection shows all drop cables are intact.
root_cause: A rogue VLAN configuration pushed via an automated script changed the native VLAN on the building's Optical Network Terminal Switch (ONTS) uplink.
resolution: 1. Roll back the configuration script on the affected ONTS device to the last known good backup. 2. Re-apply correct VLAN 110 trunking to the uplink port. 3. Monitor alarm console for device re-registration.

symptom: Subscriber calls in stating they are receiving an 'IP Address Conflict' notification on all connected devices, and network access drops every few minutes.
root_cause: The subscriber's ONT port was provisioned into an active VLAN (VLAN 44) that is already assigned to a neighboring corporate customer, causing bridging loops.
resolution: 1. Isolate the conflicting port on the OLT. 2. Provision a new, isolated VLAN (VLAN 45) specifically for this residential subscriber. 3. Flush the ARP cache on the BRAS and verify stable IP assignment.

symptom: Customer can access the internet, but their VoIP telephone adapter connected to the secondary port of the FTTH ONT has no dial tone and shows 'Registration Failed'.
root_cause: The voice profile on the ONT was associated with the data VLAN 20 instead of the dedicated VoIP voice VLAN 30.
resolution: 1. Access the ACS (TR-069) server. 2. Locate the subscriber CPE profile and update the voice WAN interface parameter to use VLAN 30. 3. Trigger a remote configuration sync and check SIP registration status.

symptom: Customer reports that speed test results show a maximum throughput of 10 Mbps despite paying for a 500 Mbps FTTH symmetrical plan.
root_cause: The traffic policing profile was correctly applied, but it was bound to an incorrect legacy VLAN 5 profile with strict bandwidth limitation profiles.
resolution: 1. Unbind the legacy profile from the OLT user-side interface. 2. Re-bind the interface to the high-speed gigabit profile utilizing VLAN 500. 3. Perform a remote speed test via TR-069 to verify full bandwidth capability.

symptom: Users on the 5G NSA secondary cell report sudden latency spikes exceeding 250ms during peak hours, severely impacting real-time video conferencing.
root_cause: X2-C interface congestion between the gNodeB and the anchor eNodeB causing control plane packet queuing.
resolution: Reconfigured QoS profiles on the backhaul link to prioritize X2 control plane traffic.
Upgraded the S1-U/X2 interface bandwidth allocation on the core router.
Monitored traffic distribution for 2 hours to ensure latency returned below 20ms.

symptom: Subscribers near the business district experience intermittent high latency (up to 400ms) and dropped packets on the 4G LTE data bearer.
root_cause: Failing optical transceiver on the primary CPRI link between the Baseband Unit (BBU) and the Remote Radio Head (RRH).
resolution: Dispatched field technician to inspect the fiber patch cables.
Replaced the faulty SFP+ optical transceiver on the BBU port 3.
Verified optical power levels and ran a bit error rate (BER) test successfully.

symptom: Complaints of high ping times (approx 180ms) for 5G FWA (Fixed Wireless Access) customers connecting through a single sector.
root_cause: Misconfigured gNodeB scheduling parameter causing excessive Hybrid ARQ (HARQ) retransmissions due to poor SINR.
resolution: Adjusted the Downlink/Uplink time slot configuration (TDD pattern) to match regional traffic demands.
Fine-tuned the antenna mechanical tilt by 2 degrees to reduce co-channel interference.
Confirmed latency normalization via automated ping probes.

symptom: Cell site experiencing generalized high latency affecting both VoLTE setup times and data packet transit over 4G.
root_cause: MME (Mobility Management Entity) pool imbalance causing signaling storms and processing delays at the local gateway.
resolution: Rerouted a portion of the tracking area subscribers to an adjacent MME pool.
Cleared the DNS cache on the serving gateway and restarted the GTP-U tunnel module.
Validated signalling response times against baseline thresholds.

symptom: Industrial park 5G private slice users report consistent 150ms latency, violating their Service Level Agreement (SLA).
root_cause: Micro-congestion on the local UPF (User Plane Function) due to unoptimized packet inspection rules in the firewall module.
resolution: Bypassed non-essential deep packet inspection (DPI) rules for the designated enterprise APN.
Scaled up CPU resource allocation for the containerized UPF instance.
Executed end-to-end latency testing confirming sub-15ms performance.

symptom: End-users notice a gradual increase in 4G browsing latency throughout the afternoon, peaking at 300ms.
root_cause: Packet buffer bloat on the microwave backhaul hop due to an outdated TCP window size configuration and queue mismanagement.
resolution: Applied Weighted Fair Queuing (WFQ) policies on the microwave modem.
Updated the firmware on the wireless bridge units to resolve buffer handling bugs.
Observed queue drop rates dropping to zero.

symptom: Tourist zone 5G network showing severe jitter and latency spikes up to 500ms during heavy tourist influx.
root_cause: Overutilization of the physical resource blocks (PRBs) on the 3.5 GHz n78 band, leading to scheduling delays.
resolution: Activated load balancing features to offload excess traffic to the overlapping 4G coverage layers.
Triggered carrier aggregation activation for capable User Equipment (UE).
Confirmed PRB utilization dropped below 80%.

symptom: Rural 4G coverage site reporting intermittent latency surges up to 600ms, causing voice call clipping.
root_cause: High packet loss and retransmissions on a degraded satellite-backed backhaul link caused by heavy local rainfall.
resolution: Switched backup routing path to the secondary microwave link.
Notified transmission provider to check satellite dish alignment and clear waveguide moisture.
Tested voice bearer path and verified jitter reduction.

symptom: Subscribers connected to Sector 2 of a 5G site experience high latency and slow DNS resolution.
root_cause: A localized memory leak in the local gNodeB DU (Distributed Unit) software stack causing packet processing delays.
resolution: Scheduled and executed a graceful reboot of the affected Distributed Unit (DU).
Monitored memory utilization graphs post-reboot to ensure stability.
Verified user plane ping times returned to normal operational limits.

symptom: University campus area 4G/5G dual-connectivity users report random 200ms latency lags when switching between cells.
root_cause: Suboptimal handover parameters (A3 offset and time-to-trigger) causing ping-pong effects and delayed path switches.
resolution: Optimized mobility parameters in the SON (Self-Organizing Networks) server for the campus cluster.
Reduced the handover hysteresis margin to accelerate inter-frequency cell transitions.
Checked drive test simulation logs to confirm reduction in failed handovers.

symptom: Internal users at Tunis-01 are unable to access the corporate intranet via its domain name, receiving a server not found error, though accessing it by direct IP works.
root_cause: A recent update to the internal BIND DNS zone file included a typo in the intranet A record, pointing to a decommissioned legacy IP address.
resolution: Corrected the typo in the zone file on the primary nameserver, incremented the SOA serial number, and reloaded the DNS service.

symptom: External clients report that our main customer portal at Tunis-02 is intermittently unreachable or resolving to a blank error page.
root_cause: The public DNS provider had a stale CNAME record pointing to an old cloud load balancer that has been retired.
resolution: Updated the CNAME record in the external DNS management console to point to the active Application Load Balancer endpoint.

symptom: Sfax-01 branch office staff cannot connect to the centralized file server by hostname, disrupting morning shift operations.
root_cause: The local Windows Active Directory DNS forwarder zone had a corrupted A record for fileserver01 due to a dynamic update conflict.
resolution: Flushed the local DNS cache, deleted the stale host record in DNS Manager, and manually recreated the correct static A record.

symptom: Automated deployment pipelines failing at Sousse-01 because the build server cannot resolve the internal artifact repository domain.
root_cause: An incorrect PTR record was added during a recent subnet migration, causing reverse lookup validation failures on the security appliance.
resolution: Corrected the IP-to-hostname mapping in the reverse lookup zone file and restarted the local resolver service.

symptom: Email delivery failures reported for outbound messages from Bizerte-01, with receiving servers bouncing mail due to authentication issues.
root_cause: The domain's TXT record containing the SPF policy had a syntax error and referenced an incorrect mail server IP range.
resolution: Validated the SPF syntax using an online checker, updated the TXT record with the correct IP blocks, and verified propagation.

symptom: Gabes-01 point-of-sale terminals are failing to sync transaction data to the regional database cluster.
root_cause: The POS VLAN DHCP scope was configured to push a legacy DNS server IP that no longer resolves the production database hostname.
resolution: Updated the DHCP scope options to distribute the correct primary and secondary DNS server IP addresses.

symptom: Nabeul-01 employees report that browsing to external HTTPS websites intermittently triggers SSL common name mismatch warnings.
root_cause: A split-horizon DNS misconfiguration caused internal recursive resolvers to return an internal proxy's IP for external domains instead of forwarding correctly.
resolution: Modified the conditional forwarders on the internal DNS appliances to bypass local overrides for external public domains.

symptom: Kairouan-01 VoIP desk phones are unable to register with the cloud PBX provider after a network reconfiguration.
root_cause: The SRV record (_sip._tls.domain.com) was updated with an incorrect port number pointing to a closed firewall port.
resolution: Corrected the port number in the public DNS SRV record from 5061 to the vendor-specified secure port 5062.

symptom: Monitoring alerts show SSL certificate expiration warnings for a service at Tunis-01, but the certificate on the web server was recently renewed.
root_cause: An outdated TXT record for Let's Encrypt DNS-01 challenge validation was lingering, causing automated renewal scripts to query the wrong verification endpoint.
resolution: Removed the stale TXT challenge records from the DNS zone and re-ran the certbot renewal script successfully.

symptom: Users at Sfax-01 experience extremely slow page load times when accessing internal web applications.
root_cause: The primary DNS server's IPv6 AAAA record for the web application pointed to an unreachable IPv6 address while the clients attempted IPv6 fallback.
resolution: Removed the erroneous AAAA record from the DNS zone until IPv6 routing is fully implemented across the site.

symptom: Customers in the northern region are reporting intermittent connectivity to international destinations, with traceroutes showing traffic looping through an unexpected third-party transit provider.
root_cause: Adjacent peer AS 65050 accidentally advertised our internal IP prefixes to the global internet, causing a massive route leak and pulling foreign traffic through our edge.
resolution: Contacted peer AS 65050 to withdraw the leaked announcements and immediately applied an outbound prefix filter on the border router to block our private space from being advertised.

symptom: Monitoring alerts show a sudden, massive spike in traffic volume entering our core routing tables from a regional customer connection, causing high CPU utilization on the edge router.
root_cause: Customer AS 65201 misconfigured their BGP policies, leaking full global routing tables into our network and overriding more specific internal routes.
resolution: Applied max-prefix limits on the customer's BGP session, shut down the peer temporarily to stabilize the control plane, and assisted the customer in correcting their route-map configuration.

symptom: Our DNS servers at this facility are experiencing degraded response times as a large portion of inbound query traffic is being misrouted via an expensive secondary transit link.
root_cause: An upstream provider erroneously prepended our AS path incorrectly, causing a partial route leak that redirected traffic away from our primary direct peering links.
resolution: Notified the upstream transit provider to fix their BGP attribute propagation and verified that local preference values on our BGP sessions were correctly tuned to favor primary links.

symptom: Internal applications hosted at the data center are unreachable from specific remote branch offices, while external internet access remains fully functional.
root_cause: A stub autonomous system connected to our edge leaked internal aggregate routes outward, creating suboptimal routing loops for specific internal prefixes.
resolution: Identified the offending neighbor via BGP summary commands, implemented strict inbound route filtering using prefix-lists, and cleared the BGP session to force a fresh table exchange.

symptom: External partners are complaining that API calls are failing and timing out when trying to reach our primary database endpoints.
root_cause: A recent maintenance window on our border gateway resulted in the accidental removal of out-bound route filters, allowing unexported customer routes to leak to tier-1 peers.
resolution: Restored the previous running configuration containing the strict route-map filters and verified via looking glasses that the leaked routes were successfully withdrawn from the global table.

symptom: Latency to cloud service providers has doubled overnight, accompanied by alerts for abnormal traffic paths on our edge monitoring dashboards.
root_cause: A transit provider leaked our more-specific /24 prefixes to an unauthorized internet exchange point, attracting suboptimal asymmetric routing paths.
resolution: Sent an urgent engineering ticket to the transit provider to rectify their AS-path filtering and applied community-based local preference adjustments on our edge routers.

symptom: Branch office staff report that enterprise voice and video calls are dropping, and traceroutes indicate packets are taking a convoluted path through an international exchange.
root_cause: An internal router re-redistributed static routes into BGP without proper tagging, causing an internal route leak that propagated to our external BGP peers.
resolution: Removed the unauthorized redistribution statement from the BGP configuration process, applied a standard route-tagging policy, and soft-cleared the BGP table.

symptom: Network operations center dashboard shows a sudden drop in traffic throughput on our primary fiber link, with simultaneous congestion on our backup backup link.
root_cause: A peer network inadvertently leaked our customer routes back to us with matching local preferences, causing a routing loop and forcing traffic onto secondary paths.
resolution: Configured an explicit 'deny own AS' rule in the BGP routing policy to automatically drop any advertised routes containing our own Autonomous System Number in the AS-path.

symptom: Certain external clients are unable to establish secure VPN tunnels to our corporate gateway, citing unreachable destination errors.
root_cause: An enterprise customer connected via MPLS leaked default routes into our BGP instance, overriding our gateway's default route and black-holing return traffic.
resolution: Configured 'no-export' community matching and strict prefix filters on the MPLS VRF interface to prevent the acceptance of default routes from the customer.

symptom: Sporadic packet loss is affecting database replication streams between our primary and secondary regional nodes.
root_cause: A misconfigured route-map on a border router allowed transit-free AS paths to leak transit traffic through our network, saturating local interface buffers.
resolution: Updated the route-map filters to strictly enforce peering agreements and limit transit advertisements only to direct customers and paid transit providers.

symptom: Customer reports intermittent drops in FTTH connection every 15-20 minutes, disrupting VoIP calls and streaming.
root_cause: High optical attenuation (-28.5 dBm) caused by a micro-bend in the indoor drop fiber near the ONT wall outlet.
resolution: Dispatch technician to re-splice the indoor fiber and replace the damaged SC/APC connector. Re-tested optical power to -19.2 dBm.

symptom: NOC alert triggered for multiple ONTs on PON port 3 going offline simultaneously for brief intervals throughout the day.
root_cause: Dirty optical connector on the OLT SFP transceiver causing intermittent packet loss and synchronization failure.
resolution: Cleaned the OLT SFP port and the corresponding feeder fiber patch cord with an One-Click cleaner. Verified optical return loss.

symptom: Subscriber experiences frequent PPP session drops during peak evening hours, requiring manual router reboot.
root_cause: BBR (Broadband Remote Access Server) interface flapping due to an unstable upstream aggregation switch link.
resolution: Replaced the faulty SFP+ module on the aggregation switch uplink and updated the port configuration to mitigate CRC errors.

symptom: User complains of random Wi-Fi and wired disconnections while the ONT LOS LED remains solid green.
root_cause: Faulty power adapter supplying fluctuating DC voltage to the ONT, causing spontaneous reboots of the device.
resolution: Replaced the defective 12V power supply unit with a new certified unit and monitored device uptime for 2 hours.

symptom: Periodic loss of synchronization on the GPON interface, correlating with high winds in the neighborhood.
root_cause: Aerial drop fiber experiencing excessive tension and friction against a tree branch, causing micro-fractures in the glass.
resolution: Rerouted the aerial drop cable using proper suspension clamps and trimmed interfering tree branches. Re-tested light levels.

symptom: Customer reports complete drop of internet service every night around 2 AM, recovering automatically after 30 minutes.
root_cause: OLT software bug causing a scheduled background process to crash the management daemon on specific line cards.
resolution: Applied vendor firmware patch to the OLT control plane and rebooted the affected line card during a maintenance window.

symptom: Frequent authentication failures and dropouts on an enterprise FTTH line using static VLAN configuration.
root_cause: Duplicate IP address assignment on the customer side causing ARP cache poisoning and gateway flapping.
resolution: Identified rogue device on the LAN, coordinated with customer IT to update network addressing, and cleared ARP table on the access router.

symptom: Intermittent broadband disconnects accompanied by severe packet loss specifically during rainstorms.
root_cause: Water ingress inside the outdoor splice closure due to an improperly sealed cable entry port.
resolution: Opened splice closure, dried the tray, re-stripped and re-spliced affected fibers, and properly sealed the enclosure with heat shrink tubing.

symptom: Subscriber notices the ONT dropping connection whenever the household microwave oven is turned on.
root_cause: Poorly shielded Ethernet cable running parallel to unshielded high-voltage power lines, inducing electromagnetic interference.
resolution: Replaced the unshielded Cat5e indoor cable with a fully shielded Cat6a STP cable and separated it from electrical wiring.

symptom: Multiple ONTs on a single splitter reporting frequent ranging errors and ranging timeouts.
root_cause: Macro-bending in the 1:16 secondary optical splitter enclosure caused by overcrowding of pigtails.
resolution: Re-organized the splitter tray management, untangled pinched pigtails, and secured cables with velcro wraps to eliminate attenuation.

symptom: Customer reports total loss of internet connection and LOS LED on the ONT is blinking red continuously.
root_cause: Fiber jumper cable inside the customer premises was sharply bent, causing high optical attenuation and loss of signal synchronization with the OLT.
resolution: Dispatched technician to replace the damaged fiber patch cord and routed the new cable safely to prevent sharp bends. Verified optical power levels are within the normal range of -18dBm.

symptom: ONT power LED is on, but PON LED is completely unlit. Customer has no service since early morning.
root_cause: A maintenance crew accidentally cut the drop fiber cable during sidewalk construction outside the building.
resolution: Spliced the severed outdoor drop cable using fusion splicing techniques and tested continuity using an OTDR. Confirmed ONT successfully registered with the GPON OLT.

symptom: Customer states the ONT keeps rebooting in a continuous loop and fails to synchronize with the optical line terminal.
root_cause: The OEM power supply unit (PSU) suffered a capacitor failure, providing fluctuating voltage that prevented the ONT from completing its boot sequence.
resolution: Replaced the faulty 12V power adapter with a new unit and tested the device stability for 15 minutes. ONT successfully synchronized and passed traffic.

symptom: NOC monitoring flags multiple offline ONTs in the same residential block. Affected customers report flashing PON lights.
root_cause: Water ingress inside the aerial distribution NAP box caused macro-bending and high attenuation on the micro-duct splitter pigtails.
resolution: Opened the NAP box, dried the enclosure, cleaned the dirty SC/APC adapter connectors with specialized optical wipes, and resealed the housing against moisture.

symptom: Customer complains of intermittent connection drops where the ONT loses sync for 5 minutes every few hours.
root_cause: The GPON transceiver inside the ONT was overheating due to poor ventilation, causing temporary laser drift and loss of frame lock.
resolution: Relocated the ONT from a closed media cabinet to an open, well-ventilated shelf and performed a warm reboot. Monitored error-free framing for 1 hour.

symptom: Subscriber reports no internet access. Upon checking, the ONT PON LED is blinking slowly, indicating a ranging failure.
root_cause: The ONT's serial number (ONU ID) was accidentally unprovisioned or mismatched during a recent OLT database synchronization script execution.
resolution: Logged into the OLT CLI, re-added the correct ONT MAC/Serial Number to the appropriate GPON profile, and forced a re-registration of the device.

symptom: Customer calls in stating their fiber modem shows a solid red LOS light and broadband is completely down.
root_cause: Micro-cracks developed in the SC/APC connector ferrule at the wall outlet due to excessive pulling force applied by the customer.
resolution: Removed the damaged wall outlet connector, stripped and re-cleaved the fiber strand, and installed a new field-assembly mechanical connector.

symptom: NOC alarm triggered for a rogue ONT causing ranging errors and service degradation for neighboring subscribers on the same PON tree.
root_cause: A malfunctioning ONT laser transmitter was stuck in the 'always-on' state (continuous transmission), causing upstream optical interference.
resolution: Identified the rogue ONT via OLT diagnostics, remotely disabled the laser output, and dispatched a field tech to swap out the defective hardware.

symptom: Subscriber reports complete loss of service. ONT status lights show power only, with no activity on LAN or PON interfaces.
root_cause: Firmware corruption occurred on the ONT flash memory during an automated midnight TR-069 firmware push, leaving the device unresponsive.
resolution: Connected a console serial cable to the ONT, forced a factory reset via emergency bootloader commands, and pushed a stable firmware image.

symptom: Customer's ONT fails to synchronize; the PON LED flashes indefinitely without achieving a steady state.
root_cause: The received optical power ($-29\text{ dBm}$) dropped below the ONT receiver sensitivity threshold due to macro-bends in the building's riser cable.
resolution: Traced the riser cable, straightened a severely pinched section inside the floor distribution tray, and verified optical power improved to $-20\text{ dBm}$.
